symbols.name: indeterminate
symbols.meaning: The indeterminate of the polynomial ring, the variable in which the packed polynomials are written.
symbols.quote: Here $y$ is the indeterminate of the polynomial ring.

symbols.name: coefficient count
symbols.meaning: The number of coefficients of each polynomial being packed.
symbols.quote: Let $r$ be the number of coefficients of each polynomial.

symbols.name: coefficient index
symbols.meaning: The index of a coefficient, running from 0 to r-1.
symbols.quote: Here $j$ indexes the coefficients, from $j = 0$ to $r-1$, so $f = \sum_{j=0}^{r-1} f_j y^j$.

symbols.name: coefficient bit bound
symbols.meaning: The number of bits in the magnitude bound on each coefficient, so every coefficient has magnitude at most 2^p.
symbols.quote: Let $p$ be the number of bits in the magnitude bound on a coefficient, so that every coefficient satisfies $|f_j| \le 2^p$.

symbols.name: packed polynomial
symbols.meaning: A polynomial in y with r integer coefficients, packed as the integer f(B).
symbols.quote: Two polynomials $f$ and $g$ in $y$ with $r$ coefficients each are packed.

symbols.name: second packed polynomial
symbols.meaning: A second polynomial in y with r integer coefficients, multiplied with f by one integer product.
symbols.quote: Two polynomials $f$ and $g$ in $y$ with $r$ coefficients each are packed.

symbols.name: block base
symbols.meaning: The base 2^{4p} of the integer encoding, one block of 4p bits per coefficient.
symbols.quote: Packing fixes a block base $B = 2^{4p}$, and replaces $y$ by $B$.

symbols.name: product polynomial
symbols.meaning: The ordinary polynomial product fg, whose coefficients are read back from the integer product.
symbols.quote: The product $h = fg$ has at most $2r-1$ coefficients, so the single integer $f(B)\,g(B)$ holds all of $h$ in its blocks.

symbols.name: centered residue
symbols.meaning: The unique integer in [-B/2, B/2) congruent to f(B)g(B) modulo B, which is the next coefficient of h.
symbols.quote: Let $c$ be the unique integer in $[-B/2, B/2)$ with $f(B)\,g(B) \equiv c \pmod B$.

relations.quote: Signed coefficient packing reduces its products to integer products, which the [Established O(n log n) multiplier](established-multiplier.md) computes.
